RelativeFarguesFontaine.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is in the libraries. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has perfectoid spaces, diamonds, v-sheaves or any Fargues-Fontaine curve, and ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E} do not exist at all; Mathlib's Witt theory is p-typical only. What does exist and is genuinely usable is upstream infrastructure: Mathlib's `WittVector` with Frobenius, Teichmuller lifts, p-adic completeness and the W(k)-is-a-DVR theorem; Fontaine's theta with surjectivity; and an absolute `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` for a single p-adically complete ring (with principality of ker theta, the theta-extension and the DVR property all still open TODOs in that file). On the geometric side Tau Ceti supplies the entire Huber-ring and adic-spectrum layer RF0 presupposes — Huber pairs, Spa(A,A+) with spectrality, rational subsets and their basis/refinement calculus, completed rational localisation A<T/s> with its integrally closed plus ring, and the identification of Spa of that pair with the rational subset — all sorry-free. Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap names: the ramified Witt algebra and its universal property, 𝒴_S and Y_S, the perfectoidness of the charts and their tilt, sheafiness, the phi-quotient X_S, Div^d and B_D, relative B_dR, O(n) and the graded algebra, and Beauville-Laszlo patching in both its linear and Tannakian forms.

targets.target: Ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E}(R) for a perfect F_q-algebra R and a nonarchimedean local coefficient field E
targets.note: Mathlib has only the p-typical `WittVector p R`, i.e. the case E = Q_p, O_E = Z_p, q = p. There is no O_E-coefficient (ramified) Witt construction anywhere: `grep -rn -i 'ramified witt\|W_\{O_E\}'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Teichmuller representatives in W_{O_E}(R)
targets.note: `WittVector.teichmuller` is the multiplicative monoid hom R ->* W(R) in the p-typical case only; the O_E-version is absent.

targets.target: Frobenius on W_{O_E}(R) (the q-Frobenius)
targets.note: Mathlib's `WittVector.frobenius` is the p-power Witt Frobenius; `frobeniusEquiv` makes it an isomorphism for a perfect base. The q = p^f Frobenius of a ramified coefficient ring is not constructed.

targets.target: pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property of W_{O_E}
targets.note: Mathlib proves p-adic completeness of W(R) for a perfect ring (`isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`) and a universal property only as the inverse limit of truncated Witt vectors (`WittVector.lift`). The strict-lift universal property (unique pi-adically complete flat O_E-algebra with W/pi = R) is not stated, in either the p-typical or the ramified case.

targets.target: Mixed-characteristic comparison with the completed scalar extension of W(-) over W(F_q)
targets.note: No comparison W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E (completed) exists; `WittVector/Compare.lean` only compares W(ZMod p) with Z_p.

targets.target: Equal-characteristic identification W_{O_E}(R) = R[[pi]]
targets.note: `PowerSeries R` exists in Mathlib but there is no Witt-vector identification with it; the equal-characteristic case of ramified Witt vectors is not formalised.

targets.target: Functoriality, reduction, topology and uniformizer-change comparisons
targets.note: `WittVector.map` gives functoriality and `WittVector.Complete` gives the p-adic topology, both p-typically. Uniformizer-change comparison has no counterpart because there is no uniformizer parameter.

duplicates.note: Layer 6.1 of the AdicSpaces roadmap packages W(O_F), Frobenius and Teichmuller lifts with the (p,[varpi])-adic topology; RF0 is the same package for a general coefficient field E.
F0 explicitly imports A_inf = W(O_F) and its (p,[varpi])-adic topology from AdicSpaces Layer 6 rather than rebuilding it; RF0 is the ramified generalisation of exactly that object.
AI.0 constructs A_inf = W(O_C^flat) with Frobenius and theta and states it reuses the common Witt-vector definitions; the p-typical part of RF0 is the same construction.
GS0:Witt-geometry says outright it will 'reuse RF0's ramified Witt algebra rather than a second coefficient ring'.

targets.target: W_{O_E}(R^+) with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology as a Huber ring
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the full Huber-ring/pair-of-definition API and Mathlib has W(R) with p-adic completeness, but nobody assembles W(O_F) (let alone W_{O_E}(R^+)) into a Huber ring with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology; the AdicSpaces roadmap itself lists this as unbuilt Layer 6 work.

targets.target: The integral period space 𝒴_S = Spa(W_{O_E}(R^+)) \ V([varpi]) over Spa(O_E)
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `spa` and its spectrality exist for an arbitrary Huber pair, but no instance is formed for a Witt ring and 𝒴 is nowhere defined. Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: The rational cover |pi|^n <= |[varpi]| != 0 of 𝒴_S
targets.note: The general theory of rational subsets and their basis property is complete in Tau Ceti; the specific annular windows of the period space are not constructed.

targets.target: Completed rational chart rings with integral-closure plus rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds A<T/s> as the separated completion of the topological localisation, defines its plus ring as the integral closure of the image of A^+ adjoined the fractions, proves it is a ring of integral elements, and identifies Spa of the pair with the rational subset. This is exactly the general construction the layer needs, but it is never applied to the Witt chart rings and nothing perfectoid is proved about them.

targets.target: FS II.1.1: after O_E -> O_{E_infty} the charts are perfectoid and their tilt glues to the perfected open unit disc over S
targets.note: There is no perfectoid ring predicate and no tilting equivalence; `PreTilt` is the inverse-limit perfection of R/p and carries none of this.

targets.target: Sheafiness of the charts by the topological direct-summand argument
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the reduction of the sheaf condition to rational covers but no sheafiness theorem at all (neither the strongly noetherian nor the stably uniform one), so no direct-summand argument can be run.

targets.target: FS II.1.2: the untilt functor 𝒴_S^diamond = S x Spd(O_E)
targets.note: Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

duplicates.note: Layer 6.1 defines exactly 𝒴 = Spa(A_inf,A_inf) minus the zero loci, with the (p,[varpi])-adic topology and rational windows, for E = Q_p and a fixed perfectoid field F.
F0 reuses Y_F = D(p) ∩ D([varpi]) and its rational annuli from AdicSpaces Layer 6; RF0:integral-Y is the relative-base, general-E version of the same space.

The perfectoidness of the chart rings after the compatible-root extension is the kind of statement P3 owns; RF0:integral-Y lists P3 as a prerequisite and re-derives the tilt computation for these particular charts.

targets.target: The generic period domain Y_S = 𝒴_S \ V(pi), the locus where pi[varpi] is invertible
targets.note: No period space of any kind is constructed in either library; `spa` is the generic adic-spectrum constructor only.

targets.target: The annulus rings with their explicit plus subrings
targets.note: The general completed rational-localisation ring and its integrally closed plus subring exist in Tau Ceti; the interval/annulus rings B^I of the period domain do not (the AdicSpaces roadmap lists them as new Layer 6.3 work).

targets.target: Complete separated sheafiness of the annulus rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the strong-noetherianness predicate and the flatness half of Wedhorn 8.28, but the Tate acyclicity/sheafiness conclusion is not proved, and nothing about B^I is.

targets.target: Restriction and completed base change for the annulus rings
targets.note: Restriction morphisms between rational localisations and the base-change isomorphism M ⊗_A A<X> = M<X> are proved in Tau Ceti in general; the annulus instance is absent. Completed tensor products over a general base are not available.

targets.target: Independence of the pseudouniformiser varpi
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines pseudouniformisers of a Tate ring, but no independence-of-varpi statement for period annuli exists.

targets.target: Sousperfectoid / stably uniform hypotheses for non-noetherian relative annuli
targets.note: Neither `sousperfectoid` nor uniform/stably uniform is defined anywhere: `grep -rn -i 'stably uniform\|sousperfectoid'` returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Fixed-field Q_p comparison identifying the existing rings
targets.note: There are no existing period rings to compare with.

duplicates.note: Layer 6.3 constructs Kedlaya's interval rings B^I, their unit balls and strong noetherianness for E = Q_p; RF0:annuli is the same construction relative and for general E.
P7's early analytic coefficient rings are the Robba-style annulus rings over a fixed field; RF0:annuli builds the same rings over a perfectoid base.

targets.target: Gluing Y_S over perfectoid affinoid covers
targets.note: Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.GlueData` glues locally ringed spaces/schemes; there is no adic-space category to glue in, and no perfectoid covers. Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: The q-Frobenius action on Y_S and its wandering annuli
targets.note: Witt Frobenius exists as a ring map in Mathlib; its action on a period space and the wandering property of annuli are not formalised.

targets.target: The adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z
targets.note: No Fargues-Fontaine curve of any kind exists in either library.

targets.target: Descent and pullback along T -> S with compatibility of structure sheaves and valuations
targets.note: Tau Ceti has residue-field valuations at points of Spa, which is the kind of datum that must be transported, but no morphism theory of adic spaces and no descent.

targets.target: Diamond formulas for X_S over Perf_{F_q} with a chosen coefficient-field embedding
targets.note: Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: Comparison of the Q_p fixed-field specialisation with FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1-F3
targets.note: Nothing on either side of the comparison exists.

duplicates.note: Layer 6.2 and 6.4 construct the wandering windows, the free phi^Z action and the quotient 𝒳 = 𝒴/phi^Z with its quotient sheaf, for E = Q_p.
F2 proves Frobenius equivariance and identifies X_F^diamond as the quotient sheaf; RF1 restates this relatively over a perfectoid base.
RF1 explicitly asks for the comparison of its Q_p specialisation with F1-F3.

targets.target: Div^d_𝒴 = (Spd O_E)^d/Sigma_d as a v-sheaf, and FS VI.1.1-VI.1.4
targets.note: Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: The completed sheaves B_D^+ and B_D = B_D^+[1/I_D] on a degree-d divisor
targets.note: Mathlib's `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` are the absolute rings attached to one p-adically complete ring R with p not a unit, built as the ker(theta)-adic completion of W(R^flat)[1/p]; there is no divisor, no relative version and no degree parameter.

targets.target: Marked untilts over E, the primitive kernel of theta and its Cartier divisor
targets.note: Fontaine's theta and its surjectivity are in Mathlib; principality/primitivity of ker theta is an explicit TODO in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean`, and there is no divisor.

targets.target: B_dR^+ filtration, residue map, graded pieces and the complete DVR at a geometric untilt
targets.note: `BDeRham.lean`'s own TODO list records that extending theta to B_dR^+ and showing B_dR^+ is a discrete valuation ring are not done; there is no filtration or residue map.

targets.target: Effective Cartier divisors of degree d, addition, disjoint loci and the symmetric-power comparison
targets.note: No divisor theory on any period space exists.

duplicates.note: This parent stage's text is the concatenation of its two substages; the divisor half is owned by RF2:integral-divisors.
The untilt and B_dR half of this parent stage's text is owned by RF2:untilts.
R06.1 constructs B_dR^+, its filtration and B_dR (plus B_cris, B_st) over a fixed field; RF2 needs the relative sheaf version of the same rings.

targets.target: Div^d_𝒴 = (Spd O_E)^d/Sigma_d as a v-sheaf quotient
targets.note: Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate). There is no Spd, no v-topology and no v-sheaf quotient.

targets.target: FS VI.1.1: the map Div^d_𝒴 -> relative degree-d closed Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S
targets.note: No relative Cartier divisors on adic or perfectoid spaces exist in either library.

targets.target: FS VI.1.2-VI.1.3: the geometric degree criterion and affineness of the divisor for affinoid S
targets.note: Absent for the same reason.

targets.target: FS VI.1.4: v-descent for bundles on the divisor and its infinitesimal thickenings
targets.note: Tau Ceti has abstract sheaves of modules with invertibility/local freeness over an arbitrary site, but no v-site and no descent theorem of this shape.

targets.target: Ordered legs: the divisor equation as a product of primitive Cartier equations, with regularity and closed image at coincident legs
targets.note: No primitive elements, no Cartier equations.

targets.target: The unordered divisor ideal descended as a line bundle
targets.note: Only the abstract notion of an invertible sheaf of modules exists.

targets.target: B_D^+ and B_D = B_D^+[1/I_D], inverse-limit completeness, gluing, restriction to Div^d_Y
targets.note: The only realisation of this pattern is Mathlib's absolute B_dR^+ = AdicCompletion(ker theta)(W(R^flat)[1/p]) and its localisation; degree, ordering-independence, gluing and restriction are all absent.

targets.target: Div^d_X by Frobenius descent, affine locally on S
targets.note: No curve X, no Frobenius descent of v-sheaves.

targets.target: The characteristic-p special fibre of the degree-one divisor giving ramified Witt coefficients
targets.note: Ramified Witt vectors are themselves absent (see RF0).

duplicates.note: F4 constructs marked untilts, the primitive kernel of theta as a closed Cartier divisor and Div^1 = Spd Q_p/phi^Z in the fixed-field case; RF2:integral-divisors is the general-E, degree-d, integral version.
GS0:loop-geometry takes Div^d_𝒴 and B_D^+ ⊂ B_D from RF2 as inputs and builds L^+G/LG over them; the two stages share the divisor rings.
HS0 imports RF2:integral-divisors for its leg divisors and formal neighbourhoods.

targets.target: Marked untilts over E and the primitive kernel of theta
targets.note: Mathlib defines theta : W(R^flat) -> R and proves it surjective for R p-adically complete with p not a unit, and `PreTilt.untilt` gives the multiplicative section. It does not prove ker theta is principal or primitive of degree one (explicit TODO in BDeRham.lean), and there is no notion of a marked untilt of a perfectoid space.

targets.target: The divisor of the untilt on Y_S and X_S; injectivity and closed image of multiplication by a local generator
targets.note: No period space, so no divisor and no annular estimate.

targets.target: Div^1 over the unramified coefficient base Spd(E-breve)/phi^Z on Perf_{F_q}
targets.note: Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: Completion along a divisor: B_dR^+ and its localisation B_dR, independent of the chosen generator
targets.note: Mathlib's `BDeRhamPlus R p` is the ker(theta)-adic completion of the localisation away from p of W(R^flat), and `BDeRham R p` inverts the generators of ker theta; both are absolute (a single ring R, hypotheses `[Fact ¬IsUnit (p:R)]` and `[IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R]`), with no divisor, no generator-independence statement and no sheaf.

targets.target: Functoriality, residue map, ideal filtration, graded pieces and base-change conditions for B_dR
targets.note: None of these is proved; the file's TODO list is 'extend theta to B_dR^+', 'B_dR^+ is a DVR', 'ker theta is principal'.

targets.target: At a geometric untilt: the complete discrete valuation ring and its residue field
targets.note: Mathlib proves W(k) is a DVR for a perfect field k of characteristic p, which is the special fibre statement, not the B_dR^+ one the layer asks for.

targets.target: Effective Cartier divisors of degree d >= 0, addition, disjoint-divisor loci, finite symmetric-power comparison with multiplicities
targets.note: Absent; no divisor theory on period spaces.

duplicates.note: F4 is the fixed-field case of exactly this stage: marked untilts, the primitive kernel of theta as a closed Cartier divisor, the annular injectivity/closed-image estimate and Div^1 = Spd Q_p/phi^Z.

P1 owns Fontaine's theta, its surjectivity, the principal non-zero-divisor kernel and the classification of marked untilts by primitive degree-one ideals; RF2:untilts consumes those and adds the divisor and completion.
R06.1 constructs B_dR^+, its filtration and B_dR over a fixed field with Galois, Frobenius and monodromy structure; RF2:untilts needs the relative version along a divisor.
AI.0 constructs theta, its kernel generator xi, and states B_dR^+ is the kernel-adic completion after inverting p — the same recipe Mathlib's `BDeRhamPlus` implements.

targets.target: O(1) by Frobenius descent with the chosen pi-normalization, and O(n)
targets.note: No line bundles on a Fargues-Fontaine curve; Tau Ceti's `SheafOfModules.IsInvertible` is the abstract notion over an arbitrary site.

targets.target: Tensor and dual comparisons O(m) ⊗ O(n) = O(m+n), O(n)^∨ = O(-n)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the tensor product of invertible sheaves of modules abstractly; the twisting sheaves on the curve do not exist.

targets.target: Divisor sections and transition functions for O(n)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The sign conversion between Frobenius eigenvalue and degree
targets.note: No degree function on bundles over the curve exists.

targets.target: The graded algebra of global sections for affinoid S, its Proj, and the analytic-to-schematic map of locally ringed spaces
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of an arbitrary graded commutative ring as a scheme, so the target of the comparison map exists in full generality; the graded algebra of sections of O(n) on X_S and the map of locally ringed spaces do not.

duplicates.note: VB2:ampleness compares bundles and cohomology on X_S with the Proj curve built here; the two stages share the graded algebra and the comparison map, and RF3 states explicitly that the ampleness/GAGA theorem belongs to VB2.
Partial overlap only: F4 builds the degree-one divisor whose sections give O(1) in the fixed-field case.

targets.target: Beauville-Laszlo gluing for finite locally free modules along a Cartier divisor
targets.note: Neither library mentions Beauville-Laszlo or formal glueing: `grep -rn -i 'beauville\|laszlo\|formal glue'` returns nothing.

targets.target: The gluing functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective, compatibly with tensor, dual, base change and several disjoint divisors
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Transfer of the gluing to G-torsors by exact tensor functors, independent of the faithful representation
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Tannakian reconstruction for affine group schemes over a field (points from tensor automorphisms of finite comodules); no G-torsor on an adic space and no tensor-functor comparison exists.

duplicates.note: The linear half of this parent stage's text is owned by the substage.
The Tannakian half of this parent stage's text is owned by the substage.

targets.target: Beauville-Laszlo gluing: a bundle off D, a bundle on the formal neighbourhood and an isomorphism on the punctured neighbourhood determine a bundle
targets.note: The ingredients (flatness, adic completion, finite projective modules) are in Mathlib, but the Beauville-Laszlo patching statement itself appears nowhere in either library.

targets.target: Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of the gluing functor
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Compatibility with tensor, dual, base change and several disjoint divisors
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Completeness, Cartier and finite-projectivity hypotheses retained for non-noetherian coefficient rings
targets.note: Mathlib's finite projective module API is non-noetherian-friendly, but the patching theorem it would feed does not exist.

duplicates.note: Overlapping: GS0's descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings is the same patching statement, taken over Div^d_𝒴.

AI.2's finite-free BKF-module classification uses 'the analytic annulus/patching arguments of BMS1 §4' and says explicitly that it reuses the existing Fargues-Fontaine patching carriers rather than rebuilding them.
BG2:smooth-Artin consumes the Beauville-Laszlo covering of Bun_G, which is the G-torsor form of this patching.

targets.target: Transfer of Beauville-Laszlo gluing to G-torsors via the exact tensor-functor comparison
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Tannakian package (reconstruction of algebra-valued points from tensor automorphisms of finite comodules, Milne §9.4) is the closest thing in either library; G-torsors on adic/perfectoid spaces do not exist at all, and the Mathlib `torsor` namespace is `AddTorsor` (affine spaces).

targets.target: Independence of the chosen faithful representation
targets.note: The Tannakian equivalence in Tau Ceti is for comodules over a commutative Hopf algebra over a field, not for bundles on a curve.

targets.target: Compatibility with extension of structure group
targets.note: Tau Ceti has fppf quotient torsors for affine group schemes, which is a genuine torsor formalism, but over Spec of a ring and not over a Fargues-Fontaine curve.

duplicates.note: BG0 constructs G-torsors on the curve and the comparison between geometric etale torsors, etale sheaf torsors and exact tensor functors Rep_E(G) -> bundles, including faithful-representation independence and extension of structure group — the same three targets. RF4:G-torsors states it only transfers the gluing along BG0's comparison.
GS0:loop-geometry imports RF4:G-torsors and restates the torsor interpretation of modifications over Div^d.
HS0 imports RF4:G-torsors for its two-bundle-plus-isomorphism stacks.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.summary: Nothing in this roadmap exists in either library, and the gap is unusually clean: 'Berkovich', 'tropicalization' in the geometric sense, 'balancing', 'Baker-Norine', 'Mumford', 'Schottky', 'Tate curve', 'Coleman integration' and 'metrized line bundle' all return zero hits across Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Mathlib's `Tropical` is only the min-plus semiring. What is available is adjacent infrastructure of real use: Tau Ceti's complete adic-spectrum layer (Spa(A,A+) with arbitrary-rank valuative points, rational subsets, analytic points, residue-field valuations, the closed polydisc with its classical points), its models of curves over a DVR with finite DVR extensions, its numerical types (the weighted dual graph with vertex genera, the arithmetic-genus formula, and Pic(T) = coker of the weighted intersection matrix, proved of rank one with finite torsion — the combinatorial Jacobian TB.3 wants), its PL/convex-polyhedron and toric-cone machinery, and the full function-field Riemann-Roch theorem. Genuinely missing is every stage's own content: the Berkovich spectrum and its comparison with Spa, the point-type classification and the skeleton metric, analytification and retraction, the graph Laplacian/specialization/slope formula and Baker-Norine, tropicalization with weights and balancing, faithful tropicalization, model metrics and measures, local heights, and Tate/Mumford uniformization with its integration interfaces.

targets.target: The Berkovich spectrum M(A) of a Banach algebra as the set of bounded multiplicative seminorms
targets.note: The word 'Berkovich' does not occur in either library: `grep -rn -i berkovich` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing. Mathlib has the bundled `MulRingSeminorm`/`RingSeminorm` that would be its points, and `WeakDual.characterSpace` is the archimedean Gelfand analogue (continuous unital algebra homs with the weak-* topology), but no nonarchimedean spectrum is formed from them.

targets.target: The topology of M(A) and its compactness
targets.note: Only the character space of a topological algebra carries a weak-* topology in Mathlib; there is no seminorm-valued analogue.

targets.target: Completed residue fields at the points of M(A)
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the residue ring and the induced valuation on the residue field of a point of Spa (`residueFieldValuation`), which is the adic counterpart; the Berkovich completed residue field H(x) is absent. Mathlib's `spectralNorm` is the norm on an algebraic extension of a nonarchimedean field, a different object.

targets.target: Gluing affinoids into Berkovich analytic spaces
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Comparison of a strictly affinoid algebra with its Huber adic spectrum by rank-one points / maximal generalizations, with continuity and the quotient topology
targets.note: The adic side is fully available in Tau Ceti — `spa` for any Huber pair, its spectrality, the analytic locus — and Mathlib has `Valuation.RankOne`, but no map from Spa to a Berkovich spectrum exists because the target does not exist.

targets.target: Retaining integral-subring and higher-rank information on the adic side
targets.note: This is a design property that Tau Ceti's development already satisfies: the plus ring is an explicit parameter of `spa` and points are arbitrary-rank valuative relations (`ValuativeRel`), never truncated to rank one. There is nothing to compare it against, though.

targets.target: Acceptance: nonclassical Gauss points on the closed disc
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the closed polydisc Spa(A<T>, A<T>°) and its classical (type-1) points and proves distinct tuples give distinct points over a field; Mathlib has the Gauss norm of a polynomial and of a multivariate power series, which is the Gauss point's seminorm. Nobody proves the Gauss point is a non-classical point of a Berkovich disc.

duplicates.note: D5 constructs the Berkovich/maximal-Hausdorff quotient functor of a diamond, which is the same rank-one-points comparison TB.0 asks for, taken in the diamond category.
DY.2 states it consumes TB.0 for 'the actual Berkovich analytic carrier', so it depends on rather than duplicates this stage.
The adic half of the comparison — Spa(A,A+), its plus ring, rational subsets, analytic points — is owned by AdicSpaces Layer 2 and is already built in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Classification of the four point types of the Berkovich affine line over an algebraically closed complete field
targets.note: The word 'Berkovich' does not occur in either library: `grep -rn -i berkovich` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing. Tau Ceti's `classicalPoint` of the closed polydisc gives the type-1 points in the adic model, with injectivity over a field, and nothing else.

targets.target: Paths and the hyperbolic metric off the classical endpoints
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Skeletons of annuli
targets.note: Tau Ceti has rational subsets of an adic spectrum, from which annuli would be cut out, but no skeleton of anything.

targets.target: Logarithmic modulus equals edge length, with the chosen absolute-value normalization
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Outgoing slopes of log norms of invertible analytic functions and their integrality
targets.note: Mathlib's `MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm` and Tau Ceti's multiplicativity of the Gauss norm on restricted series are the radius-indexed norms whose logarithms the slopes differentiate, but no slope is defined.

targets.target: Descent of the picture over a non-algebraically-closed base
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Acceptance: type IV points from nested discs with empty intersection, without spherical completeness
targets.note: Spherical completeness is not defined in either library: `grep -rn -i sphericallycomplete` returns nothing.

duplicates.note: Layer 5.4 constructs the closed and open unit discs as adic spaces and describes their points; TB.1 wants the same discs and their point classification on the Berkovich side.
DY.2's local dynamics needs the same analytic line and its point types as its carrier.

targets.target: A semistable formal model of a smooth proper curve
targets.note: Tau Ceti has models of a curve over a DVR: a flat, finitely presented total space with a chosen identification of the generic fibre, properness as a separate predicate, and the category of finite DVR extensions the semistable-reduction theorem produces. It has no semistability/nodality predicate (`grep -rn -i semistable` finds one prose mention only) and no formal models.

targets.target: The dual metric graph of the special fibre with vertex genera
targets.note: `TauCeti.NumericalType` is exactly the dual graph datum — components with multiplicities, weights, genera and a symmetric intersection matrix whose adjacency relation is required connected (Stacks 0C6Z). What is missing is the metric: no edge lengths, and no construction of a numerical type from an actual model.

targets.target: The retraction of the analytification onto the skeleton
targets.note: The word 'Berkovich' does not occur in either library: `grep -rn -i berkovich` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing. There is no analytification of a curve in either library.

targets.target: Compatibility with refinement and with finite extension of the valued field
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the category of finite DVR extensions with towers, and reindexing/equivalence invariance of numerical types, but not subdivision-invariance of a metric realisation nor base-change of a skeleton.

targets.target: Existence after the finite extension supplied by semistable reduction
targets.note: The semistable reduction theorem is not proved; the Tau Ceti StableReduction roadmap still lists it as work.

targets.target: Punctures marked and rays allowed for open curves
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Graph genus plus vertex genera recovers the curve genus
targets.note: `arithmeticGenus T = 1 + ∑ m_i (w_i (g_i - 1) - a_ii/2)` is defined and its division-free form proved, so the combinatorial side of the formula exists with the vertex-genus terms present. It is not compared with the genus of a generic fibre; Tau Ceti's `genus` is the function-field genus of a curve and no theorem links the two.

duplicates.note: That layer defines `HasNodalReduction` and proves semistable reduction after a finite separable extension, with the explicit Stacks 0CDM degree bound — exactly the input TB.2 says it obtains 'after the finite extension supplied by semistable reduction'.
Regular and minimal models over a DVR, the setting of Tau Ceti's `Model` and `NumericalType` code TB.2 would reuse.
SF.4 (deformations, models and birational geometry) is a declared input of TB.2 and owns the general model theory.
R11.3 covers semistable reduction and uniformisation for abelian varieties, overlapping TB.2's extension-of-the-valued-field statements and TB.7's uniformization.

targets.target: Divisors on a metric graph
targets.note: Tau Ceti has divisors on a function field (formal sums of places with degrees) but no metric graph and hence no divisors on one.

targets.target: Piecewise integral-affine functions on a metric graph
targets.note: Tau Ceti has piecewise-affine and PL maps between real topological vector spaces, cell-by-cell over convex polyhedra, with restriction, locality and composition. The integrality of slopes and the metric-graph domain are both absent.

targets.target: The Laplacian of such a function
targets.note: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.lapMatrix` is the combinatorial Laplacian matrix of a simple graph, not the measure-valued Laplacian of a PL function on a metric graph; it is the discrete shadow of the right operator.

targets.target: The Jacobian of a metric graph
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds `Pic(T)` for a numerical type as the cokernel of the weighted intersection matrix acting on multidegrees — precisely the critical group / discrete Jacobian of the weighted dual graph (Stacks 0C7H) — and proves it has rank one (`finrank_pic`) with finite torsion. This is the combinatorial Jacobian of a weighted graph; the metric-graph (real torus) Jacobian and its relation to divisors of degree zero are absent.

targets.target: The specialization map from divisors on a curve to divisors on the graph
targets.note: Absent; there is no graph to specialize to.

targets.target: The slope formula for rational functions
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The graph Riemann-Roch theorem (Baker-Norine)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the *algebraic* Riemann-Roch theorem for function fields in full (`exists_isRiemannRochDivisor`, Stichtenoth 1.5.15, with the canonical class, duality and degree 2g-2). Baker-Norine rank on a graph is a different combinatorial invariant and is not defined; `grep -rn -i 'baker.norine\|chip.firing\|sandpile\|criticalGroup'` returns nothing.

targets.target: The specialization inequality with its degree/rank convention
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Metrized complexes when component-curve information is needed
targets.note: `NumericalType` carries per-component genera, which is the data a metrized complex records, but there is no metrized complex.

duplicates.note: The degree/duality/positivity apparatus for curves over a DVR that TB.3's specialization inequality consumes is owned there, and Tau Ceti's `NumericalType.Pic` was built for it.
TB.5 consumes TB.3's skeleton metric and rational functions; the slope formula is shared between the two.

targets.target: Tropicalization of a subvariety of an algebraic torus by coordinate valuations
targets.note: Mathlib's `Tropical R` is only the min-plus semiring on `WithTop R` with its algebraic API (`Mathlib/Algebra/Tropical/`); there is no tropicalization map, no tropical variety and no tropical geometry.

targets.target: Initial degenerations
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'initial degeneration\|initialForm\|Newton polytope'` returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: The appropriate value-group extension
targets.note: Value groups of valuations, their transport and extension of valuations to localizations are available (Mathlib's `ValuativeRel` plus Tau Ceti's extension API); the specific divisible-hull extension used in tropical geometry is not singled out.

targets.target: The fundamental theorem of tropical geometry (Kapranov / Bieri-Groves)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'kapranov\|bieri'` returns nothing.

targets.target: Polyhedral structure, weights and balancing with irreducibility/equidimensionality conditions
targets.note: Mathlib has `PointedCone` and finite cone duality; Tau Ceti has convex polyhedra and lattice-rational toric cones and fans with subdivisions. None of this is assembled into a weighted balanced polyhedral complex, and the balancing condition is not stated anywhere.

targets.target: Pushforward of tropical cycles with lattice indices and generic degrees
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: The toric-chart and algebraic/analytic comparison apparatus TB.4 needs for its ambient torus overlaps that roadmap, whose cones/fans layer is the source of Tau Ceti's existing `Toric` code.
TB.5 is the curve case of the same tropicalization map, with the multiplicity-one criterion.

targets.target: Enough rational functions on a finite subgraph of the analytic skeleton
targets.note: The algebraic input (existence of rational functions with prescribed poles) is available through Tau Ceti's Riemann-Roch for function fields, but there is no skeleton to produce them for.

targets.target: An algebraic embedding into a toric chart whose tropicalization preserves the path metric
targets.note: Toric cones and fans exist in Tau Ceti; the embedding and tropicalization do not.

targets.target: The multiplicity-one / isometry criterion for faithfulness
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Explicit refinement when a tropicalization contracts an edge or changes the expansion factor
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Separating existence of a faithful tropicalization from a claim about every embedding
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: TB.5 is the curve case of TB.4's tropicalization with multiplicities; both need the weights and the lattice indices.
The path metric preserved here is TB.3's skeleton metric and its slope formula.

targets.target: Metrics on line bundles coming from formal models
targets.note: There are no formal models and no metrized line bundles in either library; `grep -rn -i 'metrized line bundle\|model metric'` returns nothing.

targets.target: Model measures weighted by intersection numbers on special-fibre components
targets.note: Tau Ceti's numerical types carry the intersection numbers that would weight the components (and the weighted matrix a'_ij = a_ij/w_j), but there is no measure on any analytic space.

targets.target: Functoriality and total mass equal to the algebraic degree
targets.note: Only the combinatorial total degree ∑ m_j w_j d_j of a multidegree exists.

targets.target: Semipositive metrics by controlled approximation
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Local heights with integrability and normalization
targets.note: Neither library has Weil or Arakelov heights: `grep -iP '\t[^\t]*height'` in the index returns only Lie-theoretic `heightMatrix`/`heightLevel` and similar.

duplicates.note: DY.4 says it consumes TB.6's model metrics, semipositive approximation and local measures for equidistribution; TB.6 explicitly holds back the equidistribution theorem itself.
Metrized line bundles and their heights in the Arakelov setting overlap TB.6's local analytic objects at the archimedean/nonarchimedean interface.
SF.5 is a declared input and owns the intersection theory the model measures are weighted by.

targets.target: Tate uniformization of a totally degenerate curve, with descent and the period lattice
targets.note: Mathlib has Weierstrass and elliptic curves but no Tate curve: `grep -rn -i 'tate curve\|TateCurve'` returns nothing in either tree ('Tate' in Tau Ceti means Tate cohomology or Hodge-Tate).

targets.target: The Schottky / Mumford-curve quotient in its totally degenerate range
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'mumford\|schottky'` returns nothing in either library.

targets.target: Local Coleman primitives
targets.note: Coleman integration is absent; the only 'Coleman' strings in Tau Ceti are provenance notes naming an external ChabautyColeman development for formal-group power series.

targets.target: Annular residues and monodromy
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Global path or abelian integrals, kept distinct from the local primitives
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Export of semistable graph corrections and model metrics to height consumers with actual comparison maps
targets.note: Absent; neither the graph corrections nor the heights exist.

duplicates.note: That layer owns the Tate curve over a local field (AEC VII, ATAEC IV-V); TB.7's Tate uniformization and q-period acceptance test are the same object.
R13.3 builds Tate curves and formal neighbourhoods of cusps, so the Tate-curve construction is owned twice already.
Frobenius continuation and the construction of Coleman primitives are owned by the ColemanIntegration roadmap; TB.7 only asks for handoffs.
Semistable reduction and (rigid-analytic) uniformisation of abelian varieties overlap TB.7's uniformization and period lattice.
